mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that rises above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1% or more for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines of 1% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) of at least 1% each signals a broad-based demand collapse, which depresses economic activity and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall by 1% or more in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and HOUST decline by 1% or more in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of PAYEMS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.7% for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in manufacturing activity, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months of INDPRO growth above 0.7%.
